entries.title: An absolute variation bound for weighted-star NUV walks [draft; pending w347]
entries.statement: For a finite star with at least one leaf and positive edge lengths, and a nearest-unvisited walk that stops after all vertices are visited, every random start distribution satisfies sd(L)/E L<=1/(2*sqrt(6)). For at least two leaves, write S for the sum of all edge lengths and w_1>=w_2 for the largest two. All lengths lie in [2S-w_1-w_2,2S-w_1], whose endpoint ratio is at most 3/2. A one-leaf star has constant positive length and coefficient zero. The constant is sharp over arbitrary start distributions; the uniform-start case is included but no optimality claim for that subclass is made. This does not prove an absolute bound for arbitrary graphs.
entries.proof_text:
Consider a star with m>=2 leaves, positive leaf-edge lengths w_i, total S, and largest two lengths w_1>=w_2. A nearest-unvisited walk stops when every vertex has been visited; it does not return to its start. Its length from the centre is B=2S-w_1. From leaf r it first visits the centre and then the remaining leaves in increasing edge-length order, giving L_r=2S-w_r-max_{j!=r} w_j. Ties between equal weights do not change the total length.

Hence every start length lies between A=2S-w_1-w_2 and B. Since S>=w_1+w_2 and w_1>=w_2, B>=3w_2 and B/A<=3/2. For any random start, not only the uniform law, if u=E L then averaging (L-A)(B-L)>=0 gives Var(L)<=(B-u)(u-A). Further,

    (B-A)^2/(4AB) - (B-u)(u-A)/u^2
      = ((A+B)*u-2AB)^2/(4AB*u^2) >= 0.

Thus sd(L)/E L <= (B-A)/(2 sqrt(AB)) <= 1/(2 sqrt(6)). A one-leaf star has constant length and ratio zero. This proves an absolute bound for the weighted-star class requested as a boundary case of P0255.

The constant is sharp if arbitrary start distributions are allowed: on the three-vertex star with both weights one, give the centre probability 2/5 and each leaf probability 3/10. Then L is three with probability 2/5 and two with probability 3/5, giving Var(L)/(E L)^2=1/24. Under the uniform law that same star has coefficient sqrt(2)/7; no claim of optimality within the uniform-start subclass is made.
assumptions: Positive weighted star with at least one leaf
Walk stops on visiting the final new vertex

relations.rationale: New card: "This does not prove an absolute bound for arbitrary graphs"; existing card: "For every finite positive-length graph G and a uniform initial vertex V, is sd(L_NUV(G,V))/E L_NUV(G,V) bounded by an absolute constant? Source: Aldous: The Nearest Unvisited Vertex Walk on Random Graphs,internal date26August2021, Conjecture5 and stronger Open Problem4,PDF8. Stat". This result treats an explicitly stated special case or limitation; it does not certify a solution.
New card: "endpoint ratio is at most 3/2"; existing card: "a rigorous O(sqrt(log n)) coefficient-of-variation bound follows".
